title: Correction to “Superelastic Tendon-Like Bowden Cables: Advancing Assistive Exoskeletons”
Guest Editorial: Advancements in MPC and Learning Algorithms for Legged Robots
Decoupling of hygromechanical stimuli without cross-interference enabled by distinct ion-electron charge transport
summary_zh: 研究提出了一种基于离子-电子电荷传输的独特传感机制，实现湿度与机械刺激的解耦，避免了交叉干扰，提高了测量精度。
summary_en: This study presents a sensing mechanism based on distinct ion-electron charge transport that decouples humidity from mechanical stimuli, avoiding cross-interference and enhancing measurement accuracy.
insights: 创新点：离子-电子电荷传输传感机制
方法亮点：湿度与机械刺激解耦
关键发现：提高测量精度
insights_en: Novelty: Ion-electron charge transport sensing mechanism
Method highlight: Decoupling humidity from mechanical stimuli
abstract: Accurately decoupling mechanical stimuli and environmental factors such as humidity remains a major challenge in the development of tactile sensors, as cross-interference of these stimuli in sensing signals leads to reduced measurement accuracy and reliability. To address this, we present a distinct ion-electron charge transport-driven sensing mechanism that decouples pressure and humidity under simultaneous hygromechanical conditions. To exploit the distinct charge transport kinetics of ions and electrons, we designed a biphasic dual-conductive elastomer (BiDCE). Through phase separation between ionically and electronically conductive domains, BiDCE achieves multimodal sensing ability without cross-interference between sensing signals. In addition, an impedance spectroscopy-based decoupling method, developed based on the charge transport kinetics of BiDCE, enables real-time quantification of hygromechanical stimuli. The fabricated hygromechanical sensor was integrated into a self-adaptive robotic hand, enabling the simultaneous detection of both contact (pressure) and non-contact (proximity) states of human hands and fingers. This system ensures precise grip control while maintaining safe human-machine interaction and represents a significant advancement in multimodal tactile sensors for robotic skin interfaces. Accurately decoupling mechanical stimuli and environmental factors such as humidity remains a challenge for tactile sensors. Here, the authors show distinct ion–electron charge transport kinetics, enabling cross-interference-free hygromechanical sensing for safer, adaptive human–machine interaction in robotic systems.
